caption: Kar. 8. Stela
labels: a, raised beside line number 1 at the start of the text (marks this as text a)
sic, above a sign in line 7 (kdito?wi)
reading: (1)wisi : soreyi : ḫ(2)moteliqowi : ḫdokm?(3)liqowi ñbeyrosmi : (4)tedḫlowi : peseto(5)ddokr terike(6)lowi : slẖs : kditowi : (7)ssorl : kditowi : wosi so(8)r[.]yi atomẖe pisi(9)ẖte : atmẖepisiḫ(10)rkte :
notes: Rows of the copy do not match stone lines; read right group to left group, top row down. 'wo?si' at the start: the second sign looks like 4 (i) because the top stroke of w crosses it; the same word in line 7-8 has a clear / (o). Word-final 4+w group read wi (lowi, qowi, kditowi). 'tedḫlowi' (line 4): only one sign between ḫ and lowi in the copy (/ plus small ϟ), so no e is written. Line 3-4 'ñ?beyrossi': first sign is a rising stroke with a loop and a heavy tail, ñ or d; two space-separated 3-signs before the final i. A space stands at the row break after 'liqowi' (no divider in the copy). Line 5 'kesto(5)d?nkr': first two signs S + Σ-topped long-tailed sign read ke (same shape as ke in terike), could be a; the sign after (5) is a dash with a hook, d? (or to without dot); a single dot stands before terike (written as a space). All plain closed 3-signs (sls?s?, ssorl, s in qteli/nks) default to s; m and ẖ cannot be excluded. Line 7 'kdito?wi': the sign marked sic looks like 4 with a dot below; read to? by the parallel 'kditowi' in line 6. Line 8: one hatched sign lost between r and y in soreyi. Benedictions: 'pisi' is 4,3,4 + long-tailed p in both; the end of the first, '/ϟ with bar + 3', read ẖte (could be ẖlo); in the second 'ḫrkte' the te is / + ϟ.
check_notes: All names and formula entries placed. Changes from the type: wisi (line 1), ḫmoteliqowi, ḫdokm?liqowi, ñbeyrosmi, peseto ddokr, slẖs, kditowi. The copy's /R twice proved to be o + d. Formula A type has a divider after mẖe that the copy lacks (kept). terike(6)lowi and ssorl have no conflicting entry. Index A typed 'slms' on p. 100 but the type shows ẖ.

caption: Kar. 9. Altar
labels: sic, above a sign in line 5 (teri?keoli?wi)
sic, above the dots at the end of line 13
reading: wosi : sore(2)yi : twḫi(3)qowi : kditonyeqowi tme(4)ñsel tedḫelowi aḫẖeli(5)ye : teri?keoli?wi : ḫ(6)lbiñ : p(7)esetoli(8)se qoleye(9)semlowi dseke : ms(10)senwttey stelowi : a(11)tomẖe : psoẖe?te : atm(12)ẖe psḫr(13)kete se :
notes: No raised 1 is visible at the start. Line 3 'twḫi?': the sign after ḫ is Y-shaped, read i (the hand-key's barred i form), could be ñ. 'kdii?nye': after kd (loop sign) come crossed strokes (i) and a Ꮭ-with-bar sign (i?); y is three strokes. Line 4 'ñ?': a ʌ with a cross-bar, read ñ (crossed strokes), could be d; the same sign begins line 6's last word and line 10's 'ñ?seke'. Line 5 'aḫslii(5)ye': the sign after ḫ is small ϟ + 3, read s l (could be q). 'teri?keoli?wi': the i after r is hatched; after k come small ϟ (e), / (o), large S (l) and the sic sign (4-like with a crossing stroke, read i?); expected terikelowi. Line 6 'ḫ(6)eri?ñ?': the r i pair is two hooked strokes joined by a flat tail like the i+r of terike. 'ḫ?' in line 7 is an open c with a tail (ḫ or to). Line 10 'nwttey': t is dot + hook, te is / + ϟ with bar. The divider at the start of row 9 and the end of row 11 is hatched. Line 11 'psoẖ?te': the sign after o is a heavy hatched 3-shape (ẖ? or k). Final divider marked sic. 3-signs default to s except ) read m.
check_notes: All entries placed. Index A (p. 97) typed 'pesetol lise': the copy and Index B/C have pesetolise; the ditto headword was not checked, so no correction is filed. teri?keoli?wi (line 5) has no entry and stays as read. Index B typed 'nwtety'; the type shows nwttey as in the copy.
